title: The Era of Compound Engineering — Kieran Klaassen, Every/Cora
talk_summary: Kieran Klaassen describes 'compound engineering': a human-AI sandwich loop (brainstorm → plan → work → review → polish → compound) where 50% of effort goes into extracting learnings into persistent solution documents so the autonomous middle gets better each cycle. He ships a full email product solo using a plugin (CE ideate, doc-review, brainstorm, LFG, polish, compound) that runs hours-long parallel loops and stores judgment/taste in the repo.

takeaways.technique: Solution documents in-repo as compounding memory
takeaways.what_they_do: Every repeated correction or postmortem learning is extracted into a tagged 'solution document' committed to the repo, so future runs retrieve the answer instead of re-deriving it; he claims this is net token-cheaper than re-researching.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I store all of this knowledge inside my repository as solution documents ... it's actually more token efficient in the long term

takeaways.technique: 50/50 rule: half of effort teaching the system
takeaways.what_they_do: Explicitly budgets ~50% of time to fixing what the agent got wrong by encoding it into the system, rather than only shipping the feature.
takeaways.evidence_quote: 50% of the time should go to um teaching the system for anything that it did wrong

takeaways.technique: Polish pass as 'raise the bar', separate from QA
takeaways.what_they_do: After the automated loop opens a PR, a distinct 'polish' command reviews the PR against the product (screenshots/video before-after) to raise quality, explicitly not to check correctness.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this is not QA. This is raising the bar like it should work. If it doesn't work here, your LFG flow failed

takeaways.technique: Ideate command over all open tickets/OKRs
takeaways.what_they_do: A command ingests all open issues (Linear/GitHub/Slack/Intercom) plus strategy/OKR docs and past learnings, then scores and argues what to work on next, output as a shareable HTML page.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Tell me what to do next ... it will generate uh structure from all this mess and we'll make arguments about what is good to work on

takeaways.what_they_do: Brainstorm skill deliberately asks only the minimum questions needed, because 30 questions feels productive but doesn't improve output.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It's very easy to get 30 questions and feel, "Wow, I did so much." But in the end, the goal is not to answer questions.

takeaways.technique: Long unattended parallel loops with before/after evidence
takeaways.what_they_do: An 'LFG' loop runs for hours doing plan/work/review/test, opens a PR, dogfoods, fixes, and attaches before/after screenshots/video to the PR so the human can review quickly.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It will run for hours. It will do planning work review testing. Opens a PR. It will dog food.
